notice: DB-0.5 research evidence. Not a production runtime asset. Every record here was produced by opening the document itself in session 2026-10-08 (see documents_opened.json); search summaries were not used as evidence.

claims: The primary regulator setpoint was 186 ± 4 psig while the secondary regulator setpoint was 191 ± 4 psig
tank pressures 180 / 178 psia (oxidizer / fuel) at liftoff; regulator outlet not printed
conflicts.explanation: Primary prints a single regulated value in psia; the DB-0 secondary values are psig and per-regulator. Could be design vs flight set points; not resolvable from the opened pages. Added 2026-10-28: Apollo 9 (Block II) tank pressures sit at 175-183 psia, consistent with 180 psia, but the report gives no regulator set point and says the CSM 104 regulator stems were replaced before flight (p.22). Added 2026-10-28 (second pass): the AEHS page was opened. It prints the set points as 186 ± 4 / 191 ± 4 psig and says they were referenced to a bellows vented to ambient, so in vacuum they act as about 186 / 191 psia; the units difference is a reference definition, not a disagreement. A 6 psi gap to TN D-7375's 180 psia remains (182-190 psia band), against a Tier D source citing unopened AEDC reports, so the conflict is only partly resolved.

NTRS 19860012108 p.8: the Large Throat MCC 'reduces the nozzle expansion ratio from 77.5 to 69.5:1'; nozzle unchanged. JSC-19041 §1.1.2: Block IIA introduced the larger-throat MCC; AIAA 2002-3581 lists it in the Block 2 package. So 77.5 is pre-Block IIA and JSC-19041's 2003 '77.5 to 1' is stale text. 69 vs 69.5 is rounding.

Small-throat RPL 3006 x 1.09 = 3277 ~ 3285 @109%; large throat 2,747 @RPL, 2,870-2,871 @104.5%, 2,994 @109% (2,747 x 1.09 = 2,994 DERIVED). The 1986 study's 3010 @109% is a prediction, 2,994 the flown rating.

claims: approximately 470,000 lbs vacuum / 375,000 lbs sea level @RPL

conflicts.explanation: 7,774/7,775/7,750 describe the SLS-adapted engine (insulation, new controller per FS-2015); 7,400 is a 2003 Shuttle-era approximation. Definitions are not printed. Wikipedia 7,004 lb has no primary support among opened documents. Added 2026-10-28: two more Shuttle-era sources print about 7,000 lb (Rocketdyne 1997, KSC 2006), so the Shuttle-era figures already span 7,000-7,400 lb with no definition; L3Harris's web page prints 7,775 lb against its own spec sheet's 7,774 lb.
Neither prints a power level. DB-0 news values 76,000 / 26,800 hp have no primary support.

claims: max allowable approximately 30,000 rpm; burst 38,000 rpm
conflicts.explanation: The ~30,000 rpm figure is a limit, not an operating speed. Primary operating speed found only for Block IIA at 104.5%; Block II at 109% not found. 28,120 rpm has no primary support among opened documents. Added 2026-10-28: Biggs (participant history, Tier B) gives 'almost 30,000 rpm' as the operating speed of the original 1970s engine, a third configuration.

Primary value exists only for the Block IIA (Rocketdyne) HPFTP; the Block II P&W HPFTP speed remains secondary-only. Added 2026-10-28: Biggs (Tier B) gives 35,000 rpm for the original engine's HPFTP, operating point not stated.
All are approximations or single-configuration values; 1-1.5% spread. Not reconcilable without a rated-thrust table by block.

claims: 776.3 psia 'Thrust Chamber Pressure', engine J2026 acceptance (added 2026-10-28)
conflicts.explanation: Primary manufacturer value 717 psia at nozzle stagnation for the 230,000 lb / MR 5.5 J-2. 763 psi has no support in any opened primary document; it may be an injector-face value or a different rating (not verified). R-7450-1 prints 776.3 psia for one AS-501 engine at acceptance, station unstated (its figures plot injector-end pressure): a pressure in the 760-780 psia range does exist for a 225,000 lb-class engine, but no opened document ties 763 psi to a station or rating.

claims: 2,754 lb basic engine dry; 3,492 lb including accessories
conflicts.explanation: Two primary definitions exist (basic vs including accessories). 3,480 is close to 3,492; 3,942 looks like a transposition of 3,492 (INFERRED, not verified); 3,170 matches neither primary value.

claims: AS-501 S-II five-engine average 225,362.8 lb, high mixture ratio region (flight reconstruction; added 2026-10-28)
AS-501 S-IVB engine J2031 223,278 lb, first burn (flight reconstruction; added 2026-10-28)
conflicts.explanation: Primary text confirms two ratings (225,000 lb, then 230,000 lb). Which flights used which rating, and the 232,250 lbf figure, are not established by opened documents (AEDC reports blocked). The AS-501 flight report (R-7450-1, opened 2026-10-28) shows the first Saturn V's six J-2 engines flying at about 223,000-225,000 lb at the high mixture ratio, consistent with the 225,000 lb version, but it names no rating, so effectivity is still not established by a rating statement.

claims: J-2S development bar 1965-1972; 1st 27.5:1 test 2/66; 1st 40:1 test 6/68; ready for qual 10/71; final report 3/74
conflicts.explanation: Primary timeline shows engine testing from 1966 and 40:1 configuration from 1968; '1969 first successful test' is not supported or contradicted by an opened document.

claims: Tap-off turbine drive cycle; changed to a tap-off cycle to eliminate the gas generator
conflicts.explanation: DB-0 held tap_off as SECONDARY_CLAIM only; now Tier A.
Three primary values: 1.5 Mlbf design goal, 1.530 Mlbf in the SA-503 crew manual, 1.522 Mlbf in a 2006 Rocketdyne slide. Which flights carried which rating is not established by the opened documents.

claims: combustion gasses at 5,800 °F and 1,125 psig pressure (AEHS 'One Second', Tier D; added 2026-10-28)
conflicts.explanation: Manufacturer value 1,125 psia found; the lower secondary values may be nozzle-stagnation values but no opened primary document says so. Added 2026-10-28: MSFC's AS-504 summary (Feb 1969) prints 1105 psia, also without a station; which station or epoch separates the two primary values is not established. Added 2026-10-28 (second pass): a 2013 NASA MSFC presentation prints 982 psia labelled 'ns', the usual abbreviation for nozzle stagnation. That is the first opened primary-agency document to give the lower value a station, but the slide defines neither 'ns' nor its source, so the reading is INFERRED. Added 2026-10-28 (DB-0 backlog pass): the AEHS 'One Second' page prints the manufacturer's number as 1,125 psig; a Tier D page, and it does not say whether 'psig' is deliberate, so it does not settle the station either.

claims: designed ... with a weight of 18,000 pounds
conflicts.explanation: 18,616 lb is primary but its definition (dry/burnout) is not printed; 18,000 lb is a design weight. Added 2026-10-28: MSFC's 2013 deck repeats 18,616 lb, again undefined; the AEHS page (opened, Tier D) says 'approximately 18,500 lb dry'. No primary document names the definition.

claims: normal operating point 475 psia and O/F = 5.0

conflicts.explanation: Two Tier A sources give O/F 5.0 for the RL10A-3-3A. 442.4 s is the RL10A-3-3 value in the P&W evolution table (NAP prints 442 for A-3-3); the DB-0 Purdue pairing of 442.4 s with 5.5:1 mixes variants (INFERRED). The 1966 RL10A-3-3 design report (PWA FR-1769) estimates 444 s at 5.0:1 for the A-3-3 as well, so 442 for the A-3-3 is not its design estimate; whether 442 is a later delivered value is not established. The RL10A-3-3A values are unaffected.
Confirmed as an intra-document inconsistency in the opened page. The 11 psi gap is not a gauge/absolute offset (14.7). Manufacturer data sheet unavailable (HTTP 404).

Opened Tier B source agrees with DB-0's L3Harris summary (22,300 / 451). NAP Table D-2 prints the same numbers under 'A-4-1', so the A-4-1/A-4-2 attribution is itself ambiguous. AIAA vehicle guide (450.5 s, 22.9 klbf) unreachable (404).

claims: uprate between SA-503 and SA-504 (DB-0 search excerpt)
conflicts.explanation: The SA-503 crew manual (25 Nov 1968) already tabulates 1,522,000 lb per engine, and the AS-504 summary (3 Feb 1969) gives the same 7,610,000 lb stage total, so the opened documents do not support an uprate between SA-503 and SA-504. Both documents also keep an older value (1,530,000 in the manual's prose, 1,500,000 on the AS-504 figure). Whether AS-501 and AS-502 flew at 1,522,000 is not established: no AS-501 or AS-502 document stating F-1 thrust was opened.
The AS-504 summary prints the direction the Rocketdyne slide left out: 2.27 is oxidizer to fuel (LOX : RP-1).

claims: a nominal design chamber pressure of 400 psia
Chamber pressure (throat total), psia 385.2; (injector face static) 394.6
conflicts.explanation: The introduction's 'nominal design chamber pressure' of 400 psia names no station; the estimate table gives 385.2 psia throat total and 394.6 psia injector face static at the same 15,000 lb, 5.0:1 rating. 400 psia may be a rounded specification value, but the report does not say so.

Both opened NASA documents print 425 s. The 421 s is a search summary of an encyclopedia row for two flights, never opened. The AS-501 flight analysis (NTRS 19680026222) shows why one number per flight can differ: five-engine S-II averages of 424.46 s in the high mixture-ratio region and 429.17 s after the mixture-ratio cutback, so a flight value of 421 s would describe an operating point, not the rating.

conflicts.explanation: The AEHS page gives 413.5 and 258 gallons per second, 24,810 and 15,480 gpm: the encyclopedia's 24,811 and 15,471 gpm agree to within 0.1 percent, so the two are one figure, not two. The 42,500 gpm Smithsonian figure could not be opened (HTTP 403), and neither opened page names a rating or cites a document, so whether the 5 percent gap is a rating, a pump design point or rounding is not established.
91.5 rev/s is 5,490 rpm; 5,500 is the same speed rounded. Neither page is a primary document.

claims: Engine Mass 1300 kg (2860 lbs) (June 1990, in development)

conflicts.explanation: Both opened values are for the first Vulcain: the 1990 briefing describes it in development; the ESA page describes 'the Ariane 5 Vulcain engine ... in its initial version' and gives 1686 kg.
